Inference · Sample research note

ABSTRACT

A framework for measuring inference efficiency across latency, throughput, and cost per completed task.

01

Start with the workload

The unit of comparison is a workload. Fix the model, request mix, and quality requirements before comparing configurations. Record the hardware, concurrency, prompt length, and output length so a result can be interpreted in context.

02

Measure the service

Track time to first token and time per output token alongside throughput. Report tail latency at the target load. A higher token rate is useful when requests still finish within the service’s latency budget.

03

Count completed work

Cost per completed task brings compute, retries, and quality into the same accounting. For a fixed workload, divide the serving cost by the number of requests that meet both the quality and latency criteria.

04

Keep the evidence

Record the baseline, candidate, test conditions, and any regressions. Repeat the comparison before promoting the candidate. Use the accepted configuration as the baseline for the next round.
